class.name: SteamAudioConfig
class.brief_description: Initializes and advances the global Steam Audio simulation.
class.description: Exactly one instance must be present in the running scene. It initializes [SteamAudioServer] when it enters the tree and advances simulation every physics frame. Performance settings are global allocation limits read during initialization. Configure them before this node enters the tree; changing them afterward does not resize the existing simulator and generally requires restarting the scene.

members.member: Number of directions considered when generating diffuse reflection rays. Higher values can improve real-time reflection accuracy at increased simulation cost.
The global log level for this extension. Setting it to a lower level will show more logs.
Gain applied by the default HRTF used for binaural decoding.

Maximum ambisonic order allocated for players, pathing, and reflections. Higher values improve directional detail but increase channel count, memory, and processing cost. Per-node orders are clamped to this initialized maximum.
Maximum volumetric occlusion samples allocated per source. Player values above this limit are clamped when they enter the scene.

Maximum real-time reflection impulse-response duration in seconds. Higher values preserve longer reverb tails but increase memory and convolution cost. Listener duration is clamped to this initialized maximum.

Maximum rays allocated for each real-time reflection simulation. [member SteamAudioListener.reflection_rays] is clamped to this value at startup. Higher limits permit more accurate simulation at increased CPU cost.
Maximum number of sources for which the simulator allocates real-time reflection state. Increase this when more reflected sources must be processed concurrently, at additional memory and CPU cost.
Number of worker threads allocated for runtime reflection simulation. This is separate from [member SteamAudioProbeVolume.reflection_threads], which controls offline baking.

Ray-tracing implementation used by the runtime scene. Embree may be faster for complex geometry but is unavailable on Apple Silicon, Android, and iOS; those platforms automatically fall back to Default.
